foil.title: Oil price impact from Strait of Hormuz disruption
foil.scenario_short: Oil price impact from Strait of Hormuz disruption will remain moderate over the next 30 days, with Strait of Hormuz risk at critical and oil sensitivity at 0.8, as headlines report tanker damage and oil prices topping...
foil.perspective_strategic: The critical Strait of Hormuz risk and oil sensitivity of 0.8 indicate a moderate-probability, stable market path, with the 58% confidence suggesting moderate signal reliability.
foil.perspective_contrarian: The 58% confidence level and absence of a decisive break in evidence could allow actors to contain the disruption, potentially reducing the probability below 40% if no new hard signals emerge.
foil.actor_lens: Commodity traders: Price whether stress in Middle East becomes durable over the 30d. Rebalance positions if the probability path moves away from 40%.

supply-chain-inflation.absence_reason: No maritime/inflation forecast in the feed this cycle — azimuth reports the observed energy-price facts it can see, not a disruption probability.

seismic-infrastructure.absence_reason: No product publishes a seismic forecast — earthquakes are not predictable, so there is no forecast/intel alternative to azimuth's observed USGS record. This is the honest inverse: for an observed natural-hazard fact, the sourced record IS the only trustworthy source.
